title: AI-Driven Drowsiness Detection: Enhancing Road Safety through Inclusive and Real-Time Monitoring
summary: Catalink built an AI drowsiness detector for drivers; in July 2026 its researchers reported that the models they tested generalized poorly and that phone versions fell to near chance-level accuracy.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: In a project account for the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), current as of June 2025, Catalink described a driver-monitoring prototype meant to detect fatigue across diverse users and driving conditions. The team wrote that "Current Driver Monitoring Systems (DMS) struggle to accurately detect drowsiness leading to false negatives and reduced reliability due to biases in the models." Fewer crashes and safer public transport were the intended outcomes. In a July 2025 plan, the European Union ALFIE project, which Catalink coordinates, set out to test the models in Catalink's IRIS phone app. In July 2026 Catalink researchers reported at the ITU Kaleidoscope conference that the drowsiness models they tested generalized poorly across datasets and that the versions converted for phones fell to near chance-level accuracy. The work remained offline research. No source reports a prevented crash or a change for transport operators.
purpose: Detect driver fatigue across diverse users and driving conditions.
